iPhone fixes: how they'd look

Eight fixes from the iPhone UI review (issues #1849 to #1864), and the sub-agent icon. Each shows Now, cut from the CI captures, beside Proposed, drawn in HTML at the iPhone's 375 points.

Every Proposed mock uses the two things you already chose: the desktop's flat card (#1850) and a Threads badge that counts threads that need you (#1852), so the badge reads 1, not 3. Apart from those, each changes only what its own section is about. Section 1's cards still say "Codex on Laptop · Sotto", for example, until section 5 changes that line.

Drawn with the app's own Figtree, the type scale, spacing and radii in Design.swift, and Sotto's palette from ThemePalettes.swift. SF Symbols, the status bar and the iOS switch and slider are drawn stand-ins. Where there's more than one good answer, the variants are A, B and C, and the one I'd pick is marked green.

  • 1. Cards
  • 2. Threads header
  • 3. Working card
  • 4. Permission sheet
  • 5. Meta line
  • 6. Closing sheets

#1850Cards

Each card is one fill a step off the room, as on the desktop: no ring, no top highlight, no gradient and no red stripe. Only a Needs you card glows. Working cards keep their breathing light and the runner along the bottom.

In dark the card is the theme's raised surface; in light it is the room with 4% of the text, the desktop's card. Anything drawn on a card in the raised colour steps up one, so it still shows (section 8's segment knob).

#1849Threads header

No counts line: the section headings already count. The computer menu shares the search row. Two computers that can't be reached fold into one line, "Can't reach Studio Mac and 1 more", and its Try again tries both. With one banner showing on an SE, the first Needs you card now starts in the top half.

Now · SE 375 x 667, one banner

The first card starts 430 points down, 64% of the screen.

AProposed · the menu leads the search row

BProposed · an icon menu after search

Dashed line: half of the screen. Solid line: the top of the first Needs you card.

Pick A. It puts the menu first with its name, as the regular-width layout already does, so the page still says whose threads you're seeing. B frees room for search but hides "Studio Mac only" behind an icon. At the larger text sizes A falls back to two rows, menu above search.

The fold line has no box of its own: its red light and words say it, and a box would take the 20 points that put the card in the top half.

#1854Working card

Three lines when the card has nothing new to say. A last line shows only when it adds something: background agents, the step running now where this iPhone has read the thread, or the agent's last words.

Not filedThe sub-agent icon

You said the sub-agent icon in threads looks bad without saying which one. These are the three candidates as they look now.

(1) The Agents button in a thread's top bar · person.2

Pro Max, dark, AgentsViews.swift AgentsButton. At iPhone width the button shows only its glyph, no "Agents". Separately, its count doesn't show here and the bar cuts its leading edge.

(2) A sub-agent's mark in the Agents sheet · person.crop.square

Pro Max, dark, AgentsViews.swift:361. A workflow's row takes square.stack.3d.up instead.

(3) A sub-agent step in a thread's steps · person.2

No capture shows a sub-agent step, so the second strip draws one from ThreadViews.swift (case "subagent") among the captured steps, with a stand-in glyph.

What the desktop draws. Matching it is the strongest argument here.

Users, two people: the Agents control in the tools panel (ToolsPanel.tsx). The iPhone's person.2 on (1) is the same idea.
Bot: one sub-agent, as a step in a thread's steps (ThreadActivity.tsx) and as the provider's agents still working under a reply (DelegatedWork.tsx). The iPhone draws two people on (3) and a person in a square on (2).
GitFork: a thread Sotto delegated, and "Delegated by" (DelegatedWork.tsx). The desktop's own Agents list shows each agent as a status dot with no glyph.

So the iPhone matches the desktop at (1) and differs at (2) and (3), where the desktop draws Bot.

AAs the desktop · (1) person.2, (2) and (3) Bot

BBot everywhere · (1), (2) and (3) Bot

CBranch · (1), (2) and (3) arrow.triangle.branch

Pick B. Bot is the desktop's mark for one agent, and the top-bar button shows only its glyph at iPhone width, where two people read as contacts rather than agents. B also fixes whichever of the three you meant. A is the strict desktop match, keeping two people on the button as the desktop's Agents control does. C needs no custom glyph, but the desktop uses the branch for delegated threads, not agents. Workflows keep square.stack.3d.up in every option.

I found no robot in SF Symbols, so A and B need Bot as a custom symbol in the app's asset catalog, drawn from the desktop's Lucide icon (ISC licence). Worth a look in the SF Symbols app before building. Every glyph in this section is an SVG: Bot, Users and GitFork are the desktop's own Lucide paths, and the SF Symbols are stand-ins.
